questions.q: What is the Correct Import Errors spreadsheet, and what technology does it run on?
options: A tool for deleting all staged data, running on FBDI
A reporting tool unrelated to corrections
A manual data-entry form with no spreadsheet involved
A tool, available for modules like Payables, that lets you correct rejected rows and resubmit them — and it runs on ADFdi rather than another FBDI file
questions.explain: Correct Import Errors runs on ADFdi, letting users fix rejected interface rows directly in a connected spreadsheet and resubmit just those rows.

questions.q: Why is resubmitting an entire original FBDI file, after fixing only 2 of 1,000 rejected rows, generally the wrong approach?
options: Because it is technically impossible to do
Because the 998 already-successful rows are already live records, and resending them risks duplicates or confusing errors unrelated to the actual fix
Because Oracle Fusion deletes the entire interface table automatically after each run
Because FBDI only allows one submission per day
questions.explain: Resubmitting rows that already succeeded risks creating duplicate records or triggering confusing validation errors that have nothing to do with the actual correction needed.

questions.q: What happens if a row that already successfully imported is resubmitted through the pipeline a second time?
options: It attempts to create a second, duplicate record, which validation usually (but not always cleanly) catches and rejects
It silently updates the existing record with no issue
Oracle Fusion automatically merges the two records perfectly every time
Nothing happens — duplicate submissions are always ignored with zero effect
questions.explain: A resubmitted row doesn't 'update' an already-created record — it attempts to create a new one, which can trigger duplicate-related validation issues.

questions.q: What is the correct, repeatable workflow for fixing rejected rows described in this lesson?
options: Delete the entire interface table and start the whole conversion over from scratch
Ignore the rejections and move on to the next module
Identify exactly which rows were rejected and why, correct only those specific values, and resubmit only that corrected set
Re-run the original full file every time, regardless of how many rows failed
questions.explain: The correct approach isolates and corrects only the specific rows that failed, then resubmits just that scoped set — avoiding reprocessing already-successful data.

questions.q: After resubmitting corrected rows, what should be checked?
options: Nothing further is needed once resubmission is clicked
The UCM account's storage quota
Only the original uploaded ZIP file's file size
The new execution report, to confirm the specific rows now succeeded and that no new, unexpected rejections appeared
questions.explain: Reviewing the new execution report confirms the fix actually worked and did not introduce any new, unrelated problems.
